title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 136, PD de Rham complex). The previous page asks when the functor F_A(M)=Hom_k(A,M) on k-modules can be made to 'quasi-commute' with the divided power functors Γ^p. The aim is that F_A carries divided power (PD) algebras to PD algebras. That page shows this structure is equivalent to a family of maps u_p : A → Γ^p(A) with two conditions. The first is a multiplicativity relation, u_p·u_q = c_{pq} u_{p+q}, where c_{pq} is a binomial coefficient. The second is a plethysm relation, Γ^p(u_q)∘u_p = γ^A_{pq}∘u_{pq}. Equivalently, it is a graded algebra map k{T} → Hom(A,Γ*(A)) from the divided power polynomial algebra, with an extra compatibility.

This page lists the structural data needed.
(i) The plethysm (composition) map Γ^{pq}(X) → Γ^p(Γ^q(X)). It encodes the PD axiom γ_p(γ_q(x)) = (pq)!/(p!(q!)^p) γ_{pq}(x).
(ii) The multiplication β_{p,q}: Γ^p(X)⊗Γ^q(X) → Γ^{p+q}(X).
(iii) The exponential isomorphism α: Γ*(X)⊗Γ*(Y) ≅ Γ*(X×Y). Here X×Y is the product, i.e. the direct sum, of modules.

On the coalgebra side: a comultiplication Δ: A → A⊗A and the maps u_p: A → Γ^p A. For a flat cocommutative coalgebra, u_p is naturally the iterated coproduct, landing in the symmetric tensors (A^{⊗p})^{S_p} = Γ^p A. On the functor side:
- τ_{X,Y}: F(X)⊗F(Y) → F(X⊗Y), a lax monoidal structure compatible with associativity and commutativity;
- σ^X_p: Γ^p F(X) → F(Γ^p X), a lax compatibility with Γ^p.

The point is that for a PD algebra B, Hom(A,B) becomes a PD algebra by convolution. One sets γ_n(f) = (Γ^n B → B)∘Γ^n(f)∘u_n. Grothendieck marks this 'ok ok'.

The crossed-out lower part tries a dual, naive approach. A is an algebra over k, probably of characteristic 0. Canonical maps u_n: Sym^n A → A are given by u_n(x_1…x_n) = (1/n!) x_1⋯x_n. He claims a diagram comparing C_{p+q}u_{p+q} with (u_p⊗u_q)∘Δ followed by multiplication commutes. He then notes Hom_k(Sym^n A, B) = Γ^n(Ǎ)⊗_k B for A finite projective (Ǎ the dual). A k-linear h: A → B then extends canonically to Sym^n A. This was abandoned, presumably because of the 1/n! denominators, in favour of the characteristic-free Γ/coalgebra formulation.
errors: The label β^X_{p,q} is used both for the plethysm map Γ^{pq} → Γ^p∘Γ^q and for the multiplication Γ^p⊗Γ^q → Γ^{p+q}. On the previous page the plethysm map is called γ_{pq}. This is a notational slip (the first label appears overwritten).
In the crossed-out part, u_n = (1/n!)·product needs n! invertible, i.e. characteristic 0 or a Q-algebra. This is presumably why it was struck out.
The identification Hom(Sym^n A, B) = Γ^n(Ǎ)⊗B needs A finite projective (or similar finiteness/flatness hypotheses). This is not stated explicitly.

ideas.what: Structure maps of the divided power functor: multiplication Γ^p⊗Γ^q → Γ^{p+q}, plethysm Γ^{pq} → Γ^p∘Γ^q, exponential isomorphism Γ(X⊕Y) ≅ Γ(X)⊗Γ(Y)
ideas.modern_name: Divided power algebra functor Γ (Roby); exponential property of strict polynomial functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Roby (1963, 1965); later Friedlander–Suslin (1997) strict polynomial functors

ideas.what: Characterising when Hom(A,-) carries PD algebras to PD algebras via lax monoidal and Γ-compatible structures τ, σ_p, equivalently maps u_p: A → Γ^p A satisfying multiplicativity and plethysm axioms
ideas.modern_name: Divided power coalgebra / PD structure on convolution algebras; functors lax-compatible with Γ (cf. Fresse's divided power algebras over operads)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; PD Hopf algebras and duality discussed by Berthelot, André, Fresse (2000)

ideas.what: Duality Hom(Sym^n A, B) = Γ^n(Ǎ)⊗B and canonical extension of linear maps to Sym^n
ideas.modern_name: Duality between symmetric powers and divided powers

missed.claim: A functorial formulation of 'functors commuting with divided powers', via lax monoidal plus Γ^p-lax structures, applied to Hom(A,-). It is presumably meant for PD differential operators and the PD de Rham complex. The thread is sketched but not developed on this page.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Anticipates operadic and 'Γ-functor' treatments of divided power algebras (Fresse) and the duality between PD algebras and coalgebras used in crystalline and derived PD theory. However, the content is close to known folklore.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful, characteristic-free setup of the divided power structure maps and a coalgebra-type criterion for Hom(A,-) to preserve PD algebras. This is mathematically sound but essentially standard (Roby, PD Hopf algebra duality); it is a working sketch rather than a new result.
transcription_corrections: Top label is likely γ^X_{p,q} (overwritten) for Γ^{pq}(X) → Γ^p(Γ^q(X)), not β.
Crossed-out opening likely reads 'Soit A algèbre sur un anneau k de car. 0, on définit une famille can.' — characteristic 0 matches the 1/n!.
'produit dans Sym^n(A)' is more likely 'produit évalué dans …', with the underbrace annotating x_1⋯x_n.
The left vertical arrow in the diagram is Δ: Sym^{p+q}A → Sym^pA⊗Sym^qA, and the bottom arrow is u_p⊗u_q to A⊗A.
